title: Whack-a-mole with a broken hammer: does a model internally track its automaton state?
entrypoint: whackamole/gen.py -> whackamole/cache.py -> whackamole/probe.py (also bagcheck.py, control_task.py, layersweep.py, reliabilitymap.py for the secondary claims)
primary_claim: A linear probe on Qwen2.5-1.5B activations reads a small model's internal, never-transcribed automaton state (a 6-state login DFA) correctly 88.6% of the time and outperforms order-blind baselines on order-ambiguous positions (80.8% vs 60.4% max), but the model cannot represent the count needed to distinguish 'two failures' from 'locked' (chance-level, ~50%, at every layer, even when the three-strikes rule is stated), and split-half probe testing confirms these are genuine model limitations rather than probe artifacts (only 33.8% agreement between two independently trained probes on the original probe's errors)
quote: The state is correctly read from the model's activation 88.6% of the time... Any method that sees the events and their number, but not their order, gets a maximum of 60.4%, but the probe scores 80.8% here.
metric: linear probe classification accuracy on internal automaton state
target_value: 88.6% overall (vs 76.9% transcript-only, 20% majority baseline); 80.8% on order-ambiguous positions (vs 60.4% max for order-blind methods); 50.8% on the 'two failures' vs 'locked' distinction (chance)
tolerance_rationale: headline is a compound of 6 numbers; compare the components by hand

needed: synthetic login-protocol DFA trajectories, generated entirely in-repo by gen.py

blockers: data/ (trajectories, activations, frozen probes) is explicitly gitignored - the full pipeline must be regenerated from scratch, nothing is shipped as an artifact
inspector_notes: The cleanest repo in this batch for feasibility: self-contained synthetic data generation (no external corpus to source), a small ungated model, and an author-imposed 4-hour compute ceiling baked directly into the code. High confidence this reproduces on a single 3090.
headline_artifact: figures/probe_v0.json (88.6% vs 76.9% vs 20%), figures/bag_analysis.json (80.8% vs 60.4%), figures/witness_reliability.json / figures/reliability_map.json (0.338 / max 0.623 split-half agreement)
